## What a reproduction needs {#what-a-reproduction-needs .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **The data, under a licence that allows reuse.** The OAs deposited theirs on the Harvard Dataverse under CC0, so anyone may download, use and pass them on
- **The code, or every choice that it made.** Four of the five analysts published their scripts on the OSF, and UYV3F only a review document
- **The software and its defaults.** The continuity correction of `chisq.test()` and `prop.test()`, and the base group of a factor, are part of the result
- **Someone who tries.** The SCORE reproducibility study opened a reproduction component for this paper, and it holds an empty template
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Today the class had the first three, and supplied the fourth.
:::

::: {.src}
The deposit: doi.org/10.7910/DVN/1HOVTU. The SCORE project of the paper: osf.io/3a8bg, with the robustness study at osf.io/38rsh.
:::

::: notes
The reproduction needed four things, and this case study has each of them in a form that you can check. The first is the data under a licence that allows reuse: the original authors deposited theirs on the Harvard Dataverse under CC0, which places them in the public domain, so the workshop can give you the file without asking anyone. The second is the code, or at least every choice that it made, and four of the five analysts published scripts on the OSF, the fifth a review document. The third is the software and its defaults, as the continuity correction showed. The fourth is someone who tries, and SCORE opened a reproduction component for this paper on the OSF that holds only an empty template, so nobody in the programme ran the check. [advance] Today the class had the first three and supplied the fourth.
:::

## The published model and the public file {#the-published-model-and-the-public-file .smaller}

::: {.small}
- The census codes and the continuous values of the communities would identify the housing authorities, so the public file holds **thirds** of population, ethnic composition, poverty and the HUD assessment (lower, middle, top)
- The published model, Table 1, model 3, adjusts for the continuous values: Hispanic name −0.82 (SE 0.22), *z* = `r fmt_num(mark_of("OA", "statistic"), 2)`, **`r fmt_num(mark_of("OA", "b_pp"), 1)` points**
- The same model refitted on the thirds of the public file: *z* = `r fmt_num(mark_of("OA_blinded", "statistic"), 2)`, **`r fmt_num(mark_of("OA_blinded", "b_pp"), 1)` points**, on `r mark_of("OA_blinded", "n")` replies
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Every comparison between groups of names reproduces exactly from the public file. A model with community covariates can only be approximated, by design: the file protects the authorities that were studied.
:::

::: {.src}
The ReadMe of the deposit; @EinsteinGlick2017DoesRaceAffect, Table 1; data/reference_marks.csv.
:::

::: notes
This is the limit of reproduction on this case study, and nobody is at fault for it. The housing authorities could be identified from the census codes of their communities and from the exact population, ethnic composition and poverty of each, so the public file replaces those values with thirds, lower, middle and top. The published model adjusts for the continuous values and gives a z of minus three point seven three, or twenty points, while the same model refitted on the thirds gives minus three point four seven, or a little over eighteen points. [advance] Every comparison between the groups of names therefore comes back exactly, as you have just found, and a model with community covariates can only be approximated, as the ReadMe of the deposit says. The data and the code are open, and the published number still cannot be recovered, because the public file protects the authorities that were studied.
:::
